tier_reason: The sixrs crate README (0.1.2, unchanged in 0.1.3) gives the exact commands and a shell loop (/usr/bin/time over 100 runs) with tool versions and macOS, but no CPU model and no build flags for img2sixel or chafa; it is a one-off smoke test by the author of an obscure competing crate (102 downloads, no public repo), not a well-known independent suite, so C.

corrections.caveats: The only numbers found are in the README of the sixrs crate (a competing Rust Sixel encoder by crates.io user maokangkun, crate created 2026-06-29, 102 downloads, no repository link; github.com/maokangkun/sixrs returns 404), which calls them a quick, reproducible smoke benchmark and 'workload-specific'. The measured img2sixel 1.10.5 is not a saitoha/libsixel release: saitoha/libsixel's current version is 1.8.7-r2 (May 2026), while v1.10.5 (tagged 2025-01-10) comes from the community fork libsixel/libsixel, which was archived on 2025-02-12; that build therefore predates the 2026 security fixes listed in saitoha/libsixel's 1.8.7 NEWS (CVE-2026-33018 to CVE-2026-33023 use-after-free and integer-overflow bugs, GHSA-hx93-w8p2-ffh5, GHSA-9jm7-77gr-qghv and others). Each run is a separate process on one 256x256 image, so process startup and JPEG decoding dominate (about 16 ms per img2sixel run). The options are not equivalent: img2sixel ran with -E fast (encode policy 'encode as fast as possible') and -S (--static, 'render animated GIF as a static image', irrelevant for a JPEG), while chafa's --size 256x256 counts terminal columns and rows, not pixels (chafa man page; pixel modes default to --scale 1.0). chafa wrote a 35x larger output (4,248,878 vs 121,993 bytes), so the tools do different work (dithering, palette, compression). CPU model and the libsixel and chafa build flags are not given. libsixel's own README, NEWS and docs carry no benchmark numbers; the README only claims improved compression over older encoders.

notes: Numbers verified verbatim (img2sixel 1.64 s, sixrs 1.66 s, chafa 7.32 s for 100 runs; output bytes as recorded); the 4.5x over chafa is derived from page data and is a tie with sixrs. Shortcomings to record: the benchmarked img2sixel 1.10.5 is the archived libsixel/libsixel fork's release, not saitoha's 1.8.7 line; startup-dominated per-process timing; non-equivalent options (chafa --size in cells, 35x larger output); the record's gloss of -S was wrong (it is --static); many 2026 memory-safety CVEs fixed in saitoha/libsixel 1.8.7. Metadata checked: MIT, 2.9k stars, last commit 2026-06-15, not archived.

tier_reason: Bar labels in resvg v0.8.0's perf-oxygen.svg and perf-elementary.svg match the record exactly; the v0.8.0 README states no CPU, compiler, flags or librsvg build and links no script (the AMD 3700X, tmpfs and resvg-test-suite tools/perf script appear only from v0.9.0, whose charts drop librsvg). A competitor's README chart, and a later third-party issue report without hardware or versions, so C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Oxygen 4.12: librsvg 2.45.5 163 s versus resvg 0.8.0 cairo 195 s, qt 191 s, raqote 205 s, skia 175 s (about 1.2x faster than resvg-cairo, derived from page data); QtSvg 5.12.3 160 s. Elementary 5.0: librsvg 24 s versus resvg qt 35 s and QtSvg 30 s, but resvg cairo, raqote and skia need only 19 s (librsvg is slower there). A third-party user report on current versions (linebender/resvg issue #1146, 2026-10-01, clip-path-heavy Illustrator-style SVG): rsvg 42 ms versus upstream resvg 960 ms at 1000 px wide and 537 ms versus 31.7 s at 4000 px (about 23x and 59x, derived from page data); a patched resvg in the same report took 18 ms and 437 ms, faster than rsvg.
corrections.caveats: Numbers are bar-chart labels in two SVG images (perf-oxygen.svg, perf-elementary.svg) in the resvg 0.8.0 repository, measured by the resvg author (a competitor, independent of librsvg). The same README says all tested applications have different SVG support, which impacts the performance, that Chrome, Firefox, Inkscape and Batik were left out for startup time, and that librsvg wins on Oxygen because it has a faster Gaussian blur and uses native cairo clipping, which the resvg author calls incorrect but faster, so part of the win comes from a less correct clip implementation. v0.8.0 states no CPU, compiler flags or librsvg build configuration and links no script (the v0.9.0 and v0.9.1 READMEs name an AMD 3700X, single thread, tmpfs, script in resvg-test-suite/tools/perf, but those charts dropped librsvg), so the tier is capped at C. librsvg 2.45.5 dates from 2019 and the resvg cairo, qt and raqote backends no longer exist. librsvg loses to resvg on the simple Elementary set (24 s versus 19 s) and QtSvg is as fast on Oxygen (160 s) only because it skips filters, clipPath, mask and pattern. The only current comparison reached is linebender/resvg issue #1146 (open, 2026-10-01, one pathological clip-path file, no hardware, versions or flags, AI-assisted analysis) where resvg's per-clip layer allocation makes it 23-59x slower than rsvg; a proposed resvg patch beats rsvg there. These are the same v0.8.0 charts already used as the evidence for resvg (wave 10, which lists librsvg as its baseline), read in the opposite direction. A WebSearch snippet (page not opened, blocked) mentions a later table with rsvg 2.42.2 at 242 s versus Inkscape 0.92.4 at 1610 s and Batik 1.12 at 3686 s on the W3C suite; not used in the record. The GNOME wiki, gitlab.gnome.org and librsvg's own rsvg-bench were not reached; the repo_url is the read-only GitHub mirror (canonical home is gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/librsvg). Same chart README: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RazrFalcon/resvg/v0.8.0/README.md and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RazrFalcon/resvg/v0.8.0/.github/perf-elementary.svg

notes: Chart numbers verified exactly; tier C stands. Shortcomings to record: mixed result (faster than resvg only on blur and clip-heavy Oxygen, slower on Elementary, tied with feature-poor QtSvg), resvg's README attributes part of librsvg's Oxygen lead to incorrect native cairo clipping, 2019 versions with no hardware or harness, and the same charts are resvg's (wave 10) evidence in reverse. Added the current third-party resvg issue #1146 numbers (rsvg 23-59x faster on a clip-path file) to claimed_speedup. Metadata checked: LGPL-2.1-or-later (workspace Cargo.toml), 410 stars on the mirror, last commit 2026-10-01.
